name: Square One District Block 22 /97–101 City Centre
status: On hold · optional dated 2021 roof/podium reference
geometryCoverage: Optional dated 2021 reference; current exact geometry and roof-height relationship unverified
modelCaveat: approximation of HPA A 100/A 003 revision 3, April 23 2021, not a current approved or as-built design. A 100 shows stepped podium roofs and tower terraces that the retained flat municipal proxies omit. The actual north roof contours are extracted from drawing vectors. Intermediate tower outlines are inferred by fitting the A 003 plate-area programme and A 100 setback directions; the southern intermediate profiles reuse the shared typology as a mirrored inference. Both green roof surfaces are actually source-vector-traced; the southern rooftop envelope is adjusted to contain its supplied roof outline. Ground podium coverage and enclosed volume below each roof remain approximate without floor plans. Window spacing/frames and finishes are reference approximations; no current facade schedule was supplied. Printed roof EL 335.55/365.55 and roof/height comparisons suggest an additional 7.5 m roof enclosure above the quoted 175.25/205.25 m heights, but elevations/sections and Burnside C 200 revision 5 are needed to confirm the grade, height definition and ASL interpretation. The source-based study uses those printed roof levels and an inferred EL 152.80 grade; it does not silently change the project catalogue heights. Mechanical/mezzanine and typical-floor elevations are inferred to fit the total, not measured levels. Open roof zones are retained and no exposed basements are exported. Roads are untouched. The applications remain open and applicant-paused, not officially cancelled; no start or completion timeline is confirmed.

Ground-floor west/east bodies follow the latest publicly linked original ground drawing, dated October 3, 2024, cross-checked against the March 2026 site-plan entrance arrangement. This lower-level revision remains less certain. Eight entrance-column centres come from that ground drawing; 0.6 m diameters are illustrative. No structural engineering accuracy is claimed. Contours follow the actual settlement diagram rather than stretching a superseded City model. The height-zone surfaces are independently extruded; coincident hidden surfaces remain. Cladding, railings, detailed balconies, structural openings and landscaping are not inferred. Building base is the median sampled Ontario DTM grade, not a legally calculated or approved established grade. Relative maximum heights are taken verbatim from the governing diagram. February 2025 approval is in principle, with the final order withheld pending conditions and draft zoning schedules subject to City technical review. No later complete architectural set was publicly recovered. The settlement specifies a 12-storey slab, replacing the former 15-storey/17-with-rooftop tower. The slab has a 42 m maximum and the delineated mechanical/amenity area a 48 m maximum. The rooftop mechanical/amenity footprint extends to the western boundary in the source diagram; its permitted envelope is modelled above the 42 m slab, with that overhang retained. Thin same-height stepback lines on the 42 m area are retained only as the overall maximum envelope because the zoning graphic does not assign separate floor elevations to them.

modelCaveat: Approximate marketing-plan-derived townhome envelopes, not surveyed architectural models. Seven June footprints and three additional highlighted blocks in the currently linked image are registered through two City street junctions and four common roof centroids. The image scale bar conflicts with City junction spacing by about 25%; City coordinates control the model scale. Estimated placement ±10 m and roof-outline tolerance ±3 m are interpretive, not statistical confidence bounds. The ten retained envelopes use an estimated 13 m maximum with ±3.5 m uncertainty, derived from about 6.2 m registered bay width and roughly 2.1:1 height-to-bay proportions in the official illustrative facade. No published dimensional height was found. Roofs, balconies, basements and facade articulation are omitted; grey marketing roofs are retained from the June version, not independently confirmed current building drawings. Five additional grey roof envelopes shown in Caivan’s June 2026 marketing plan, registered using the unchanged two-junction transform of the retained ten-envelope model. All five lie inside City parcel 33912100. Three eastern rows lie within current SP 25/68 W 1 (Block 8, 88 townhouses); two western contextual rows lie outside the reviewed current application polygons and have no verified active-file assignment. The grey background artwork is not a final architectural drawing or confirmed construction phase. Use as explicitly uncertain future context. The 13 m display height remains the original Aura estimate with ±3.5 m uncertainty; placement ±10 m and outline ±3 m remain interpretive bounds. No number of dwellings, exact metre height, occupancy date, detailed roofs or final facade is inferred from these envelopes. Existing ten-envelope geometry remains unchanged.
